lessonRef.title: Performance task build: analyzing real decisions, policies, and games

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $12 and Option B has expected payoff $7. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning two faces to each.
choices: Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A game costs $15 to play. It pays $12 with probability 1/4 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $-3; the game is unfavourable to the player
$-12; the game is unfavourable to the player
$3; the game is favourable to the player
$-15; the game is unfavourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $6 and pays out $570 with probability 1/190. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $35 and Option B has expected payoff $52. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.

items.prompt: A game costs $24 to play. It pays $78 with probability 1/6 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $13; the game is favourable to the player
$54; the game is favourable to the player
$-11; the game is unfavourable to the player
$-24; the game is unfavourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $39 and pays out $334 with probability 1/167. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
